$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Compute Engine. One entry per console section; level per substrate (nano = shared core, also dev_server/unified ingress; offline = appliance). Proven by tests/conformance/test_capabilities.py — a claim the backend does not honour fails CI.

gcp.compute.instances.crud.title: VM instances (create, start, stop, suspend, resume, reset, delete)

gcp.compute.instances.data_plane.title: Guest OS access (SSH, screenshot, OS info)
limitations: SSH: no SSH daemon runs behind an instance — there is no guest OS to open an interactive shell on.
Screenshot: getScreenshot needs a real virtual display's framebuffer; none is rendered, so there is nothing to capture.
OS info: getGuestAttributes is populated by a guest agent writing back through the metadata server after boot; no guest OS or agent runs to report hostname, OS release or kernel version.

gcp.compute.instances.serial_console.title: Serial port output
limitations: Serial output is Vyomi's own instance lifecycle record (create/start/stop/suspend/resume/reset, each at its real timestamp) rendered as console lines, not a real guest kernel's boot/console text — no guest OS runs to produce authentic kernel or init messages.

gcp.compute.images.crud.title: Custom images (create from disk, import rawDisk from Cloud Storage, export to Cloud Storage, import/export history)
limitations: Import (images.insert with rawDisk.source) really checks the .tar.gz object exists in the simulator's Cloud Storage; export writes an image archive (tar.gz with image metadata) into a real destination bucket object. Disk CONTENTS are not modeled, so neither moves guest bytes.

Export, and the import/export history (global/imageJobs), are Vyomi collections: real gcloud compute images import|export run Cloud Build workflows and show up as Cloud Build history, which Vyomi does not run.

gcp.compute.instance_groups.crud.title: Instance groups (unmanaged and managed)
limitations: Autoscaling policies aren't simulated — there's no real request load for a policy to react to, so resize (manual, or a rolling update's own batch of creates/deletes) is the only way the member count changes.

gcp.compute.observability.title: Observability, recommendations and VM Manager
limitations: The status duration and recent-activity feed shown here are real — Vyomi's own recorded instance lifecycle operations (insert/start/stop/suspend/resume/reset/...) at their real timestamps — not Cloud Monitoring charts or Cloud Logging entries: there's no request-metering engine tying a VM's real CPU/disk/network state to a sampled time series (the same boundary as gcp.storage.observability).
Recommender suggestions are state-derived (see gcp.compute.recommender), not Google's usage-based AI insights.
VM Manager (Patch, OS policies, VM Extension Manager) needs a guest OS and patch agent to apply anything to — none runs in Vyomi.

gcp.compute.recommender.title: Recommender (Compute Advisor, dashboard recommendations)
limitations: Recommendations are computed from live Compute state only (unattached disks, in-use disks without any backup, unused reservations, unattached resource policies, empty sole-tenant node groups). There is no CPU/memory/network utilisation telemetry, so Google's usage-based recommenders (idle VM, rightsizing machine type) are not produced.
Idle-disk recommendations fire immediately on an unattached disk; the real recommender observes it for ~14 days first. Savings are estimates from list prices, not your billing data.
Applying a recommendation is manual: markClaimed/markSucceeded/markFailed/markDismissed record state, nothing is auto-remediated.

gcp.compute.instance_schedules.title: Instance schedules (scheduled VM start/stop)
limitations: Schedules are evaluated lazily on every Compute API call (no background thread in a substrate-independent core): fire times missed while the appliance/browser tab was not running are caught up (last 24 snapshot fires, the most recent start/stop) at the next call instead of firing at their wall-clock minute.
Time zones need the host's tz database; on a runtime without one (some in-browser Python builds) schedules evaluate in UTC.

gcp.compute.snapshot_schedules.title: Snapshot schedules (hourly / daily / weekly with retention)
limitations: Schedules are evaluated lazily on every Compute API call (no background thread in a substrate-independent core): fire times missed while the appliance/browser tab was not running are caught up (last 24 snapshot fires, the most recent start/stop) at the next call instead of firing at their wall-clock minute.
Scheduled snapshots are metadata records (size is the disk's provisioned size, not changed blocks); there is no incremental block storage to snapshot.
Application-consistent (guest flush) snapshots need a guest agent; `guestFlush` is stored but not honoured.

gcp.compute.instant_snapshots.title: Instant snapshots
limitations: Instant snapshots are zonal metadata records of a disk (name, source, size); no block data is captured, so a restored disk is an empty disk of the same size.

gcp.compute.async_replication.title: Disk async replication
limitations: Replication pairing, constraints (cross-region, size, unattached secondary) and lifecycle are real, but disks hold no block data here, so nothing is copied and there is no measured RPO/replication lag; state is always ACTIVE until stopped.

gcp.compute.consistency_groups.title: Disk consistency groups
limitations: A consistency group is a diskConsistencyGroupPolicy resource policy attached to disks; group-wide crash-consistent snapshotting and group failover are not performed because no block data is replicated.

gcp.compute.instances.multi_nic.title: Multiple network interfaces
limitations: Up to 8 NICs in distinct VPC networks are stored and returned (nic0..nicN, per-NIC internal IP); packet forwarding between NICs and per-NIC routing are not simulated (no guest network stack).

gcp.compute.instances.lb_health_check_fi.title: Load balancer health-check firewall rule
limitations: The console creates a real VPC firewall rule (130.211.0.0/22, 35.191.0.0/16 on the chosen ports, target tag lb-health-check) and tags the instance; there is no load balancer sending health probes.

gcp.compute.network_endpoint_groups.title: Network endpoint groups
limitations: Zonal, global (internet) and regional serverless NEGs with endpoint attach/detach/list and validation are real; endpoint health is not reported and a NEG cannot be attached to a backend service because no load balancer data plane exists.

gcp.compute.reservations.title: Reservations
limitations: Capacity is not actually held back: reservations are accounting. Running VMs whose machine type and zone match (and whose reservationAffinity allows it) are counted as consumers up to the reserved count, but a VM is never refused for lack of unreserved capacity.
Shared reservations (shareSettings) are stored, not enforced across projects.

gcp.compute.sole_tenant.title: Sole-tenant nodes (node templates, node groups, node types)
limitations: Node groups, templates and VM-to-node placement (first-fit by vCPU and memory, with a hard fit check at VM creation) are real; there is no physical host, so maintenance policies and autoscaling are stored but never act, and CPU overcommit is not modelled.

gcp.compute.storage_pools.title: Hyperdisk Storage Pools
limitations: Pool capacity accounting (a disk can't exceed free provisioned capacity; ADVANCED allows 5x thin provisioning) and disk-type matching are enforced; provisioned IOPS/throughput are stored but disks are not throttled by them (there is no I/O path).

gcp.compute.rollouts.title: Rollouts
limitations: Compute rollout plans orchestrate Google-managed product updates across waves; there is no managed fleet or update stream to roll out.

gcp.compute.security-risk-overview.title: Security risk overview
limitations: Findings come from a deterministic rule engine over the project's real stored VMs and firewall rules (public IP, full-API-access default service account, OS Login / serial port / project SSH keys, Secure Boot, IP forwarding, firewalls open to 0.0.0.0/0 for SSH/RDP/all ports, with the instances each rule affects). It is not Security Command Center: no Trivy/vulnerability scanning of guest OS packages, no threat detection, no attack-path simulation, and no findings history or muting.

gcp.compute.migrate-to-vms.title: Migrate to Virtual Machines (source connectors, replication, cut-over)
limitations: Migrate to Virtual Machines replicates running VMware / AWS / Azure machines through a source connector appliance and delta-syncs their disks before cut-over; Vyomi has no source hypervisors to connect to and no replication engine. To bring a disk archive in, use Import VM (a .tar.gz in Cloud Storage -> image -> instance), which is simulated.

gcp.compute.incidents.title: Google Cloud incidents (service health feed)
limitations: The feed reports outages on Google's real infrastructure; Vyomi is a local simulator with no Google status source, so there is nothing true to report.

gcp.compute.tpus.title: TPUs (Cloud TPU nodes / queued resources)
limitations: TPUs are Google-proprietary accelerator hardware with no software equivalent that could run XLA workloads in the simulator.

gcp.compute.bms.title: Bare Metal Solution (servers, networks, VRFs, volumes, NFS shares, procurements, maintenance events)
limitations: Bare Metal Solution provisions physical Oracle-certified servers in a Google-colocated facility with procurement and on-site maintenance workflows; there is no hardware (or meaningful software stand-in) to model.

gcp.compute.committed-use-discounts.title: Committed use discounts (purchase)
limitations: A commitment is a billing contract with Google (1 or 3 year term, charged to a billing account); Vyomi bills nothing real, so purchasing one would only create a record with no effect. The cost meter prices on-demand usage only.

gcp.compute.capacity-advisor.title: Capacity advisor (zonal capacity and obtainability forecasts)
limitations: Forecasts are derived from Google's live fleet-wide capacity telemetry, which a simulator does not have; Vyomi can create resources in any zone without capacity limits.

gcp.compute.preview-features.title: Preview features (opt-in to pre-GA Compute Engine features)
limitations: The catalog and enrollment are managed by Google per project and gate real backend rollouts; Vyomi has a single fixed feature set.
